correctness.rationale: For every positive clique and independent-set size, the six initial-color cohorts remain monochromatic. At a resting clique vertex the omission of its own (nonexcited) state makes the common excited-neighbor count equal to the total excited mass on both shores, while resting independent vertices see only excited clique mass. Truncating each fixed cohort mass to 0, 1, or 2 preserves all threshold-two comparisons at every update, even after initial cohorts merge in color. Thus 26 squared = 676 admissible signatures rigorously represent all labelled configurations, with identical first-periodic-entry time and eventual primitive period. The certificate contains all 676 trajectories and the included verifier recomputes each, confirming sole periods 1 and 3, first entry at most five, the count and sharp witness at time five, and the rotating-period-three onset inequalities. The exhaustive tiny quotient is sufficient for arbitrary graph sizes because of the proved exact reduction, not because of finite graph-size extrapolation. The exponential generating function formula follows by six labelled cohort multinomial factors. A separate literal edge-neighbor implementation exhaustively agrees for 221436 labelled configurations and six exact population comparisons. The probabilistic limit follows from the event of at least two vertices of each color in the clique and a three-color union bound. Scientific limitations: graphs must be complete split graphs with synchronous three-state threshold-two update. No independent audit is asserted.

value.rationale: This classifies the infinite natural family of complete split graphs under a classical threshold-excitation operator with a sharp phase diagram, sharp universal five-step entry bound, exact six-cohort labelled basin census and mathematically motivated one-sided clique-pacemaker probability law. Completing one bipartite shore into a clique removes every primitive four-cycle while permitting three-cycles with only one independent vertex (when clique has at least five vertices), a qualitative graph-topology effect not derived by merely recomputing a known table. The probability bound tends to one uniformly in independent-side size, explaining the new oscillatory mechanism beyond finite examples.
